name: 46,XX Difference of Sex Development Induced by Fetoplacental Androgens Excess
aliases: 46,XX DSD due to Fetoplacental Androgen Excess

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XX DSD Induced by Fetoplacental Androgens Excess

criteria.description: Presence of varying degrees of genital virilization in a 46,XX individual
Confirmed 46,XX chromosomal pattern without SRY gene presence
Biochemical evidence of elevated fetoplacental androgen levels during gestation or elevated androgen metabolites postnatally
Exclusion of other common causes of 46,XX DSD such as congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Imaging showing presence of normal internal female reproductive organs (uterus, ovaries)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of genital virilization in a 46,XX individual with biochemical evidence of fetoplacental androgen excess and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on clinical, biochemical, and genetic evaluation with exclusion of other DSD etiologies.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of the clitoris due to androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion of the labia resembling scrotum
Presence of uterus and ovaries despite external virilization

common.notes: Underdevelopment or shortening of the vaginal canal
External genitalia not clearly male or female
Increased circulating androgens detected in blood tests
searchTerms: high male hormone levels after birth

common.symptomName: Normal female secondary sexual characteristics at puberty
common.notes: Development of breasts and menstruation despite early virilization
searchTerms: normal breast and hair development at puberty

occasional.notes: Excessive hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to genital ambiguity
occasional.notes: Emotional and psychological impact of DSD
searchTerms: psychosocial issues due to unclear genitalia
mental health impact of ambiguous genitals

rare.notes: Rare cystic lesions in clitoral tissue
Elevated blood pressure possibly linked to androgen effects
searchTerms: high blood pressure from androgen excess
raised blood pressure due to androgens

laboratory: Elevated serum androgens (androstenedione, testosterone) in neonatal period
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound or MRI showing normal uterus and ovaries
genetic: No mutations in CYP21A2 or other CAH-related genes
other: History of maternal or placental conditions causing androgen excess
Exclusion of maternal androgenic drug exposure

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated serum androgens in older child or adult

redFlags: Severe genital ambiguity requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Signs of salt-wasting crisis excluded but must be monitored
Psychosocial distress or gender identity concerns requiring specialist support
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Consensus statement on DSD. Pediatrics. 2006.
Orphanet Report: 46,XX difference of sex development induced by fetoplacental androgens excess. Orphanet 2024.
